newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Police battle Islamists during Bangladesh strike.
newsitem.headline: Police battle Islamists during Bangladesh strike.

text.p: Police fired tear gas and wielded batons in pitched battles with hundreds of militant Islamists in the Bangladesh capital Dhaka during a general strike on Tuesday, witnesses said.
Dozens of people were injured in the clashes and scores arrested, they said.
The violence occurred throughout the city, they added. Supporters of the strike hurled homemade bombs and stones at security personnel and attacked mini-taxis carrying journalists.

Militants chased a bus which had taken to the streets early on Tuesday in defiance of the strike. Six people were seriously injured after the bus, trying to flee the scene, overturned and was hit by a police van, witnesses told reporters.
Police detained around 100 protesters in Dhaka, they said.
Dhaka and the rest of the country came to a virtual halt as Moslems responded to a general strike called by radical Islamic groups.
Offices and schools were closed and available transport was limited to a few rickshaws.
Trading was suspended at the country's two stock exchanges in Dhaka and Chittagong and other businesses were also closed.

"There is no activity taking place here today. The streets are empty, except for hundreds of white-robed Islamic mullahs marching and chanting," said one journalist in the southern industrial town of Khulna.
"Life has been totally disrupted in this city of over one million people," said one official in Chittagong.
Handling of cargo was mostly suspended at Chittagong and Mongla ports, port officials said. The Bangladesh airline Biman said it operated only a few flights with few passengers.
Rail transport was badly disrupted as strikers barricaded tracks at many places, one railway official in Chittagong said.

The Islamists called the dawn-to-dusk strike across the country to protest against a right-wing Jewish woman in the Israeli town of Hebron who two weeks ago plastered storefronts with posters portraying the Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig.
They said the act "ridiculed and defamed" Mohammad.
Nearly 90 percent of Bangladesh's 120 million people are Moslems.
Moslem anger also was stirred up after Palestinians said Israeli troops ransacked a school and tore up copies of the Koran.
"The strike is intended to voice our strongest protest against attempts to ridicule the Prophet by blasphemous acts of an Israeli Jewish woman," said a leader of the Jamaat-e-Islami party.
"True Moslems can never tolerate the outrageous act and the devilish courage to dishonour (Prophet) Mohammad," a leader of the radical Islamic Constitution Movement said.
Hundreds of angry Islamists on Monday burned Israeli flags in Dhaka and called for a "Jihad (Islamic holy war) against the Jews".
Strike supporters also exploded dozens of homemade bombs in the city on Monday night. Police said no one was injured.

The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) led by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia and the Jatiya Party of former military ruler Hossain Mohammad Ershad gave the strike their support.
The ruling Awami League -- and a few smaller Islamic groups -- opposed the strike, saying it was unwarranted after the Bangladesh parliament adopted a unanimous resolution condemning the blasphemy.
